_comment: The STATE of every round-4 finding. The narrative stays in docs/open-defects.md; this is what the index table is rendered FROM, so a count cannot drift from the rows. Optional fields (severity, inviolable, class, attempts, blocked_by, next_attempt_requires, pins, disposition) are OMITTED rather than guessed — fill one in when a slice touches that finding and knows the answer. An entry that HAS attempts must satisfy the D5 rule: open + >=2 attempts requires blocked_by and next_attempt_requires.

findings.summary: telemetry beacons counted as causal writes (fixed ON the branch)
the causal set REPLACED the temporal set (fixed ON the branch)
cross-origin seq collision rebinds a gate — not attempted
a swallowed drain rebinds commits to the next step — not attempted
a page-synthesised commit launders a deferred write; **HIGH**, inviolable #3; two fix attempts failed, D5 gate applies

attempts.outcome: over-refused an APG role=button activated by ENTER — recordable by mouse, refused by keyboard

attempts.shape: require a trusted activation to have begun the turn
attempts.outcome: forgeable: form.requestSubmit() and checkbox.click() yield TRUSTED events from a bare task

findings.next_attempt_requires: a new SENSOR CLASS, not a better inference — isTrusted is ruled out entirely (it means the user agent fired the event, and a page can make the user agent fire events), as are navigator.userActivation and driver-side tagging. A human-verdict sensor is a verdict VERB plus a TRIGGER that puts the question in front of a human; specifying only the verb built half a sensor once already (0.92.0 provenance + 0.93.0 flow mark left R4.5 exactly where it was).

findings.summary: the matrix asserted only that SOME step is gated — closed by S1
`recordWire` bypasses `pushRec`, so wire markers have no in-memory fallback
nothing pinned the AUGMENT-NEVER-REFUSE rule (pinned only on the parked branch)
`test_run_cached_refuses_it_too…` no longer exercises its stated property
the H9 judge captured and judged write flows — closed in 0.82.0
post-auth-refresh `write_unreadable` falls to the generic tail, recorded ok=False
`_learn` takes no `pre_write`, so learn-time write verification is a bare presence check
`release()`'s gating read has no provenance
`audit_flows`' candidate loop had no per-flow guard — closed in 0.80.0 (S7a)
`cli._flow_dispatch` lets `MetaUnreadableError` traceback on six verbs — closed in 0.95.0 (S10)
a refusal pairs the NEW recipe with the PREVIOUS read_pin/shape/steps_hash
a quarantine's value-free reason is replaced by a bare IO error — closed in 0.95.0 (S10)
`_save_meta`'s failure surfaces as a bare OSError every handler misses — closed in 0.95.0 (S10)
`_reset_learn_baselines` clears shape/contracts but not `read_pin`
seven durable renames, one retry — closed in 0.95.0 (S10) by one shared `fsio` helper
`record()`'s refusal stays non-terminal — deliberate, but each retry re-fires the write
Windows `ERR_NO_BUFFER_SPACE`, **9 occurrences**; socket churn refuted at 0.104.0; occurrence 8 (local) argues local ≠ CI, and occurrence 9 landed on a DOCS-ONLY PR with a failing-run capture
`test_flows_dry_run_holds_a_real_write_flow` failed once under load, undiagnosed
a localhost round-trip stalled past the 5 s budget; ships unmitigated, 2 occurrences
the load-dependent "cluster of three" was one defect + one bad test — assertion fixed in 0.88.0
the recorder credited a DEFERRED write to the next click — closed in 0.88.0
the wire promotion marks ordinary GraphQL-style READS as writes (12/12 measured)
`_write_owner` turns confident when a neighbour's grace tail expires — observation, harmful direction not reproduced
a deferred write ESCAPED the learn watcher (removed with no drain) — closed in 0.96.0 by draining the remaining act window
a commit deferred beyond `write_window_ms` is still unobserved — the residual R4.29 does not close; needs an over-refusal measurement first
an unrecognised `mode` fell through to LEARN — re-authored the flow and RE-FIRED its write; closed in 0.98.0
every failed replay returned an EMPTY `note` while the cause sat in the traces; closed in 0.98.0
the corpus row added to adjudicate R3.7 could not fail for it — closed in 0.101.0 by the `row-nested-icon` scenario
a shared `aria-label` on a nested per-row container turns the row guard OFF → silent wrong-row bind; **HIGH**, inviolable #3
a heal on a ROW-GUARD refusal re-grounds to a byte-identical recipe and reports a repair that repairs nothing
a write leaving in a LATER dispatch was credited to the last commit — NARROWED in 0.105.0 (direct-`fetch` shape closed), see R4.38
a control whose nested wrapper owns no identity captures no `anchor_id`, so the row guard silently does not run; **HIGH**, inviolable #3
`ACTIVATION_CAUSED` matches an event's TYPE NAME with no provenance, so a write laundered through a synthetic `submit`/`reset` re-enters attribution; **HIGH**, inviolable #3
the wire Idempotency-Key is whichever step was mid-act, so a deferred write's key moves with PAGE TIMING and a retry cannot dedupe; **HIGH**, inviolable #3
`_learn` snapshots straight after navigate with no settle floor, so a client-rendered page is authored against its unrendered skeleton — quiet, and one variant PERSISTS a refusal
the SDK choke-point pin allowlists `vision.py`, which does NOT route through `build_client` — so the inference the test states does not hold and `no_llm` would not intercept a vision call

`flow release` returns "nothing to release" before `release()` runs, so the remedy `flow.py:207` names is dead through the CLI — and WIDENING the status check does not reach the cached-recipe shape (measured) — FIXED at 0.109.0 by DELETING the pre-check (reshape-plan 1.2); `release()` now returns a ReleaseResult and the CLI reports what it cleared

`_SDK_CTORS` does not match `genai.Client()`, so gemini's construction is invisible and the anti-vacuity floor is met by exactly 3 — which also makes R4.41's own remedy misdiagnose itself — FIXED at 0.4a (PR #179): `Client` added to `_SDK_CTORS`, anti-vacuity floor raised 3 -> 4 measured, `GenerativeModel` kept so the old API stays covered
B1: a raised attempt drops its own LLM spend, traces and minted keys, and leaves `ok`/`failure_code` stale from the previous attempt (F2 guarded the relearn leg only)
B1: `record.usage == {}` on the miss / escalate / precheck / pre-attempt-refusal / raise exits, against `RunRecord`'s own "always populated" docstring
B1: a usage-less later attempt flips a priced total to `None` with no reason flag — a missing key and an unpriceable one are treated alike
B1: the FAILED-path cell asserts one default and two truthy values, so an engine populating the record only on success keeps it green
B1: eleven wiring mutations of the record plumbing survive the entire suite — only two cells pass `record=` at all
B1: `record.failure_code` speaks the internal `kind` vocabulary, not `FlowReplayError.code`, and can name a different attempt than the exception
B1: `llm_calls` / `traces` / `healed_steps` / `total_ms` exclude the relearn while `usage` includes it, so two fields disagree about one run
B1: the "a 0-LLM replay says observed zero" claim has no end-to-end pin — an engine reporting UNKNOWN on every replay passes every cell
B1: `BatchRowResult.landed` is the two-state bool the same PR calls a trap, reading `False` on successful write rows and on crashed rows
B1: a key-less teacher (`ScriptedProvider`/`MockProvider`) is classified as an unobserved SPENDER, contradicting `flow.py:915-916`; `accounting_failed` is sticky across runs
the key scrub's completeness rests on a hand-written variable list (Bedrock/Vertex uncovered) — the shape S14 replaced with a derivation
the key scrub is in-process only: on win32 an empty value is an ABSENT one, so a child process would re-read `.env` while both pinning cells stay green

a fixture sub-resource silently fails to load and surfaces as a JS `ReferenceError`; the HTTP/1.0 socket-churn cause is REFUTED by measurement (8 vs 6 connections per load) and a sweep would risk 8 hangs — disposition is the shared fixture server
findings.disposition: reshape-plan step 0.7 (shared fixture server) — explicitly NOT a protocol sweep

findings.summary: a SUCCESSFUL run reports the failed attempt's `failure_code` — `_attempt_replay`'s success exit sets `ok` but never clears it, and `_mark_ok` (which does) is only called on the precheck and relearn exits; found by the exit-set matrix on its first run
findings.disposition: reshape-plan step 1.5 (the single-exit RunRecord sink) — not a fourth _mark_ok call site

findings.summary: the R4.22 resource sampler measures the wrong quantity: a Windows shard failed TWICE on two DIFFERENT browser tests, both latency-shaped (a 5s Locator.wait_for timeout; a write confirm missing inside its budget), while the same run's PASSING Windows shard was the MORE loaded of the two on 4 of 7 sampled metrics — the first same-run healthy baseline, and it refutes resource exhaustion for this symptom class. Neither CPU nor disk I/O is sampled, which is what a latency failure is about
findings.disposition: add CPU and disk-queue sampling before the next occurrence is diagnosed; do NOT re-derive the socket/handle hypotheses, which this measurement rules out for timeouts
